basic_info: Katherine, 22 months old, female, presented for kidney ultrasound due to geneticist's concerns related to her Smith-Magenis syndrome.
present_illness: No specific symptoms reported yet; evaluation for potential kidney issues based on genetic concerns. Katherine has been noted to pee a lot and drink a lot. She goes through a lot of wet diapers in a day, maybe around 8 to 10. She seems to pee a lot, and I think she drinks a lot too. She used to only drink milk, but we switched to pea protein milk and now she also drinks water sometimes with a little juice. I don’t think she has any discomfort or urgency when she pees.
past_history: Smith-Magenis syndrome diagnosed due to developmental delay (not walking or sitting by herself at a year old). Family history of kidney issues or genetic disorders: none. Chromosomal deletion associated with Smith-Magenis syndrome, which can be linked to leg and kidney issues.
aux_exam: No prior kidney function tests (blood work or urinalysis) reported. No previous imaging studies of her kidneys or urinary tract before today.
